claim: Intracellular levels of the amino acid aspartate are responsive to changes in metabolism in mammalian cells.
source: Intracellular levels of the amino acid aspartate are responsive to changes in metabolism in mammalian cells and can correspondingly alter cell function, highlighting the need for robust tools to measure aspartate abundance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general observation about aspartate metabolism.

claim: Changes in intracellular aspartate levels can alter cell function.
source: Intracellular levels of the amino acid aspartate are responsive to changes in metabolism in mammalian cells and can correspondingly alter cell function, highlighting the need for robust tools to measure aspartate abundance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general observation.

claim: jAspSnFR3 has a 20-fold increase in fluorescence upon aspartate saturation as a purified protein.
source: As a purified protein, the sensor has a 20-fold increase in fluorescence upon aspartate saturation, with dose-dependent fluorescence changes covering a physiologically relevant aspartate concentration range and no significant off target binding.
evidence: This is reported as a measured property of the purified sensor protein in the abstract.

claim: jAspSnFR3 shows dose-dependent fluorescence changes covering a physiologically relevant aspartate concentration range.
source: As a purified protein, the sensor has a 20-fold increase in fluorescence upon aspartate saturation, with dose-dependent fluorescence changes covering a physiologically relevant aspartate concentration range and no significant off target binding.
evidence: This is reported as a measured property of the purified sensor protein in the abstract.

claim: jAspSnFR3 has no significant off-target binding.
source: As a purified protein, the sensor has a 20-fold increase in fluorescence upon aspartate saturation, with dose-dependent fluorescence changes covering a physiologically relevant aspartate concentration range and no significant off target binding.
evidence: This is reported as a measured property of the purified sensor protein in the abstract.

claim: When expressed in mammalian cell lines, jAspSnFR3 sensor intensity correlated with aspartate levels measured by mass spectrometry.
source: Expressed in mammalian cell lines, sensor intensity correlated with aspartate levels measured by MS and could resolve temporal changes in intracellular aspartate from genetic, pharmacological, and nutritional manipulations.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result in the abstract.

claim: jAspSnFR3 can resolve temporal changes in intracellular aspartate from genetic manipulations.
source: Expressed in mammalian cell lines, sensor intensity correlated with aspartate levels measured by MS and could resolve temporal changes in intracellular aspartate from genetic, pharmacological, and nutritional manipulations.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result in the abstract.

claim: jAspSnFR3 can resolve temporal changes in intracellular aspartate from pharmacological manipulations.
source: Expressed in mammalian cell lines, sensor intensity correlated with aspartate levels measured by MS and could resolve temporal changes in intracellular aspartate from genetic, pharmacological, and nutritional manipulations.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result in the abstract.

claim: jAspSnFR3 can resolve temporal changes in intracellular aspartate from nutritional manipulations.
source: Expressed in mammalian cell lines, sensor intensity correlated with aspartate levels measured by MS and could resolve temporal changes in intracellular aspartate from genetic, pharmacological, and nutritional manipulations.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result in the abstract.

claim: Mass spectrometry coupled with gas chromatography or liquid chromatography requires highly specialized equipment.
source: This approach is powerful but has significant drawbacks; it requires highly specialized equipment, it is expensive, and sample preparation by chemical extractions homogenizes metabolic differences that may occur among different cells in complex samples or across subcellular compartments.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of MS-based approaches.

claim: Mass spectrometry-based metabolite measurement is expensive.
source: This approach is powerful but has significant drawbacks; it requires highly specialized equipment, it is expensive, and sample preparation by chemical extractions homogenizes metabolic differences that may occur among different cells in complex samples or across subcellular compartments.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of MS-based approaches.

claim: Sample preparation by chemical extractions homogenizes metabolic differences that may occur among different cells in complex samples.
source: This approach is powerful but has significant drawbacks; it requires highly specialized equipment, it is expensive, and sample preparation by chemical extractions homogenizes metabolic differences that may occur among different cells in complex samples or across subcellular compartments.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of MS-based approaches.

claim: Sample preparation by chemical extractions homogenizes metabolic differences across subcellular compartments.
source: This approach is powerful but has significant drawbacks; it requires highly specialized equipment, it is expensive, and sample preparation by chemical extractions homogenizes metabolic differences that may occur among different cells in complex samples or across subcellular compartments.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of MS-based approaches.

claim: Biosensors provide subsecond and subcellular resolution for visualizing metabolite dynamics.
source: Development of genetically encoded protein sensors (biosensors) over the past two decades has provided new opportunities to visualize the release, production, and depletion of important signaling molecules and metabolites with subsecond and subcellular resolution (reviewed in Kostyuk et al., 2019; Koveal et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a known capability of biosensors, supported by citations.

claim: Aspartate is among the most concentrated metabolites in cells.
source: Aspartate is among the most concentrated metabolites in cells (Park et al., 2016), yet it is one of only two amino acids that is not predominantly acquired from the environment.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Aspartate is one of only two amino acids that is not predominantly acquired from the environment.
source: Aspartate is among the most concentrated metabolites in cells (Park et al., 2016), yet it is one of only two amino acids that is not predominantly acquired from the environment.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about aspartate metabolism.

claim: Glutamate is made from glutamine by the enzyme glutaminase.
source: While the other, glutamate, is made from glutamine by the enzyme glutaminase, no analogous enzyme exists in humans to convert asparagine to aspartate (Sullivan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about glutamate metabolism.

claim: No analogous enzyme exists in humans to convert asparagine to aspartate.
source: While the other, glutamate, is made from glutamine by the enzyme glutaminase, no analogous enzyme exists in humans to convert asparagine to aspartate (Sullivan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Aspartate must be synthesized by transamination of oxaloacetate by the cytosolic enzyme GOT1 or the mitochondrial enzyme GOT2.
source: Instead, aspartate must be synthesized by transamination of the tricarboxylic acid cycle metabolite oxaloacetate by the cytosolic enzyme GOT1 or the mitochondrial enzyme GOT2.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about aspartate synthesis.

claim: Aspartate synthesis can occur from multiple metabolic sources via complex metabolic reactions occurring in both the cytosol and mitochondria.
source: Notably, aspartate synthesis can occur from multiple metabolic sources via complex metabolic reactions occurring in both the cytosol and mitochondria, rendering aspartate levels at the whole cell and subcellular levels dependent on multiple metabolic variables.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about aspartate metabolism.

claim: Impairments to mitochondrial respiration can deplete aspartate levels.
source: For example, impairments to mitochondrial respiration can deplete aspartate levels and aspartate restoration can reestablish proliferation in cells with defective mitochondria (Sullivan et al., 2015; Birsoy et al., 2015; Cardaci et al., 2015; Hart et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Aspartate restoration can reestablish proliferation in cells with defective mitochondria.
source: For example, impairments to mitochondrial respiration can deplete aspartate levels and aspartate restoration can reestablish proliferation in cells with defective mitochondria (Sullivan et al., 2015; Birsoy et al., 2015; Cardaci et al., 2015; Hart et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to stem cell function.
source: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to cell function in multiple biological processes, including stem cells (Tournaire et al., 2022; Arnold et al., 2022), immune cells (Bailis et al., 2019), endothelial cells (Diebold et al., 2019), and cancer (Helenius et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to immune cell function.
source: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to cell function in multiple biological processes, including stem cells (Tournaire et al., 2022; Arnold et al., 2022), immune cells (Bailis et al., 2019), endothelial cells (Diebold et al., 2019), and cancer (Helenius et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to endothelial cell function.
source: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to cell function in multiple biological processes, including stem cells (Tournaire et al., 2022; Arnold et al., 2022), immune cells (Bailis et al., 2019), endothelial cells (Diebold et al., 2019), and cancer (Helenius et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to cancer cell function.
source: Alterations to aspartate levels are associated with modifications to cell function in multiple biological processes, including stem cells (Tournaire et al., 2022; Arnold et al., 2022), immune cells (Bailis et al., 2019), endothelial cells (Diebold et al., 2019), and cancer (Helenius et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Genetic methods to elevate intracellular aspartate can increase tumor growth.
source: In addition, genetic methods to elevate intracellular aspartate can impact biology in vivo, increasing tumor growth (Sullivan et al., 2018; Garcia-Bermudez et al., 2018) and improving hematopoietic function (Qi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Genetic methods to elevate intracellular aspartate can improve hematopoietic function.
source: In addition, genetic methods to elevate intracellular aspartate can impact biology in vivo, increasing tumor growth (Sullivan et al., 2018; Garcia-Bermudez et al., 2018) and improving hematopoietic function (Qi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: iGluSnFR was developed using the E. coli glutamate/aspartate-binding domain (GltI) linked to circularly permutated GFP.
source: We have previously developed a biosensor for glutamate (iGluSnFR) using the E. coli glutamate/aspartate-binding domain (GltI) linked to circularly permutated GFP (Marvin et al., 2013), and subsequently optimized it by modulating its affinity, kinetics, color, and total fluorescence change (SF-iGluSnFR and iGluSnFR3) (Marvin et al., 2018; Aggarwal et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: The GltI domain binds both glutamate and aspartate, with lower affinity for aspartate than glutamate.
source: Since the GltI domain also binds aspartate, albeit at lower affinity than glutamate (Hu et al., 2008), we reasoned that subtle modifications to the ligand-binding site could switch the relative aspartate/glutamate specificity.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: S72A and S72P mutations were identified as having switched specificity from glutamate to aspartate.
source: By expressing mutant sensors in bacteria and measuring the fluorescence of bacterial lysate in response to aspartate and glutamate, we identified S72A and S72P as having switched specificity from glutamate to aspartate.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result.

claim: S72T mutation also preferentially binds aspartate over glutamate.
source: S72T, identified in a faster version of iGluSnFR (Helassa et al., 2018), also preferentially binds aspartate over glutamate.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: jAspSnFR3 is yellow shifted in excitation and emission compared to typical GFP-based sensors.
source: Further characterization of the sensor found it is yellow shifted in excitation and emission compared to typical GFP-based sensors, since its chromophore is formed by the triad of GYG and has the T203Y pi-stacking mutations of the Venus yellow fluorescent protein.
evidence: This is reported as a measured property of the sensor.

claim: jAspSnFR3 does not appreciably change its green fluorescence in response to other amino acids.
source: The sensor also does not appreciably change its green fluorescence in response to other amino acids (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) or to other decoys considered relevant to aspartate metabolism, including pharmacological treatments (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: The mRuby3 fluorescence of affinity-purified jAspSnFR3-mRuby3 responds to some amino acids at high millimolar concentrations.
source: Surprisingly, the mRuby3 fluorescence of affinity-purified jAspSnFR3.mRuby3 responds to some amino acids at high millimolar concentrations, indicating a non-specific effect (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.

claim: The mRuby3 response to amino acids is due to an unexpected interaction with the C-terminal histidine tag.
source: This was determined to be due to an unexpected interaction with the C-terminal histidine tag and could be reproduced with other proteins containing mRuby3 and purified via the same C-terminal histidine tag (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B, C).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental finding.

claim: jAspSnFR3 is unaffected by temperature up to 37°C.
source: Our aspartate sensor appears unaffected by temperature up to 37°C, with the same maximum ΔF/F at 37°C as compared to 30°C (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result.

claim: A recently described aspartate sensor is adversely affected by temperatures higher than 30°C.
source: A recently described and concurrently developed biosensor for aspartate is reported to be adversely affected by temperatures higher than 30°C, causing lower maximum ΔF/F (Hellweg et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to another study.

claim: jAspSnFR3 is sensitive to pH.
source: Like all cpGFP-based sensors, it is sensitive to pH but changes in fluorescence due to aspartate far exceed what one might expect from changes in fluorescence due to physiologically attainable changes in intracellular pH (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated as a known property of cpGFP-based sensors with experimental data.

claim: 24 hr of glutamine withdrawal abolished GFP signal in H1299 jAspSnFR3 cells while leaving RFP unchanged.
source: Indeed, we found that 24 hr of glutamine withdrawal abolished GFP signal while leaving RFP unchanged.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.

claim: Rotenone treatment causes a dose-dependent decrease in jAspSnFR3 sensor fluorescence in H1299 cells.
source: Titrating rotenone in H1299 cells, we observed a dose-dependent decrease in sensor fluorescence with increased rotenone, corresponding to the expected decrease in aspartate synthesis capacity, and a partial restoration of fluorescence in cells co-treated with pyruvate (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Pyruvate co-treatment partially restores jAspSnFR3 fluorescence in rotenone-treated H1299 cells.
source: Titrating rotenone in H1299 cells, we observed a dose-dependent decrease in sensor fluorescence with increased rotenone, corresponding to the expected decrease in aspartate synthesis capacity, and a partial restoration of fluorescence in cells co-treated with pyruvate (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Pyruvate can rescue aspartate levels after an initial depletion phase with rotenone.
source: Furthermore, we tested and confirmed the ability of pyruvate to rescue aspartate levels after an initial depletion phase with rotenone, thus confirming that the sensor is also able to measure the reverse kinetics of aspartate restoration (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result.

claim: H1299 GOT1/2 DKO cells are unable to synthesize aspartate and are dependent on aspartate uptake from the media.
source: To this aim, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to generate an H1299 cell line with a double knockout (DKO) of the genes glutamic oxalacetic transaminases 1 and 2 (GOT1/2 DKO), which renders cells unable to synthesize aspartate and therefore dependent on aspartate uptake from the media (Garcia-Bermudez et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: In H1299 GOT1/2 DKO cells, sensor fluorescence decreased upon aspartate withdrawal, approaching a steady state after approximately 11 hr.
source: Using these H1299 GOT1/2 DKO cells, we titrated media aspartate and observed that sensor fluorescence decreased upon aspartate withdrawal, approaching a steady state after approximately 11 hr, that corresponded to the aspartate availability in the media (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: 10 mM media aspartate is unable to rescue sensor signal significantly above aspartate depleted media in H1299 GOT1/2 DKO cells.
source: We note that 10 mM media aspartate, a higher concentration than any other amino acid in media, is still unable to rescue sensor signal significantly above aspartate depleted media.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.

claim: Aspartate has poor cell permeability and often requires concentrations of 20 mM or more to robustly contribute to intracellular aspartate pools.
source: This confirm previous observations that aspartate has poor cell permeability and often requires concentrations of 20 mM or more to robustly contribute to intracellular aspartate pools (Sullivan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Glutamine withdrawal from H1299 cells showed a rapid depletion in sensor fluorescence with a low-level steady state reached after approximately 12–16 hr.
source: Glutamine withdrawal from H1299 cells showed a rapid depletion in sensor fluorescence with a low-level steady state reached after approximately 12–16 hr (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: Glutamine repletion after depletion caused an initial rapid increase in sensor fluorescence followed by a slower adjustment phase before reaching baseline.
source: In the same cells, glutamine repletion, after different times of glutamine depletion, caused an initial rapid increase in sensor fluorescence followed by a slower adjustment phase before reaching baseline.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.

claim: Cells remain viable 12 hr after glutamine withdrawal.
source: These data confirm that cells remain viable 12 hr after glutamine withdrawal and that proliferation rates are first fully recovered when aspartate levels reach baseline.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: Proliferation rates are first fully recovered when aspartate levels reach baseline after glutamine repletion.
source: These data confirm that cells remain viable 12 hr after glutamine withdrawal and that proliferation rates are first fully recovered when aspartate levels reach baseline.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: Metformin is a commonly used diabetes treatment that acts as a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor.
source: Metformin is a commonly used diabetes treatment that has been shown to act as a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor (Owen et al., 2000; El-Mir et al., 2000; Andrzejewski et al., 2014; Wheaton et al., 2014) and can decrease intracellular aspartate levels in a dose responsive way (Gui et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Metformin can decrease intracellular aspartate levels in a dose responsive way.
source: Metformin is a commonly used diabetes treatment that has been shown to act as a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor (Owen et al., 2000; El-Mir et al., 2000; Andrzejewski et al., 2014; Wheaton et al., 2014) and can decrease intracellular aspartate levels in a dose responsive way (Gui et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Metformin is hydrophilic and poorly permeable to most cells, resulting in comparatively delayed kinetics for metformin to decrease mitochondrial respiration in intact cells.
source: Whereas rotenone is a lipophilic molecule that can cross the cell membrane and act rapidly, metformin is hydrophilic and poorly permeable to most cells, resulting in comparatively delayed kinetics for metformin to decrease mitochondrial respiration in intact cells.
evidence: This is stated as a known property of metformin.

claim: The aspartate depleting effects of metformin acted slower than rotenone.
source: We observed that the aspartate depleting effects of metformin acted slower than rotenone, with 30 nM rotenone reaching steady state after ∼20 hr and 2 mM metformin reaching a similar sensor response after almost 40 hr.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.

claim: Oligomycin A binds to and inhibits the proton-coupled rotation of ATP synthase.
source: Oligomycin A binds to and inhibits the proton-coupled rotation of ATP synthase (Symersky et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Oligomycin inhibition leads to a slowing of the electron transfer in the mitochondrial electron transport chain by hyperpolarizing the membrane potential.
source: This inhibition leads to a slowing of the electron transfer in the mitochondrial electron transport chain by hyperpolarizing the membrane potential (Brand and Nicholls, 2011) and it has previously been shown that the cellular effects of oligomycin can be rescued by partial uncoupling of the mitochondrial membrane potential (Sullivan et al., 2015; To et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: The cellular effects of oligomycin can be rescued by partial uncoupling of the mitochondrial membrane potential.
source: This inhibition leads to a slowing of the electron transfer in the mitochondrial electron transport chain by hyperpolarizing the membrane potential (Brand and Nicholls, 2011) and it has previously been shown that the cellular effects of oligomycin can be rescued by partial uncoupling of the mitochondrial membrane potential (Sullivan et al., 2015; To et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Oligomycin induces a decrease in aspartate that can be partially restored by the mitochondrial membrane potential specific uncoupler BAM15.
source: We used our aspartate sensor to show that oligomycin induces a decrease in aspartate and that the mitochondrial membrane potential specific uncoupler BAM15 (Kenwood et al., 2014) can partially restore this aspartate level (Figure 2G), thus confirming previous observations and illustrating the versatility of the our sensor.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: Asparagine becomes essential upon glutamine starvation.
source: It has previously been reported that asparagine, a product of aspartate metabolism, becomes essential upon glutamine starvation (Pavlova et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Full glutamine depletion has a rapid and drastic effect on jAspSnFR3 sensor signal.
source: One solution to this problem is to measure the temporal changes in aspartate levels over the course of glutamine starvation and, indeed, we found that full glutamine depletion has a rapid and drastic effect on sensor signal (Figure 2E, H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental result with references to figures.

claim: Aspartate signal did not robustly correlate with the concentration of glutamine in the media in the short term.
source: Interestingly, aspartate signal did not robustly correlate with the concentration of glutamine in the media in the short term, but instead we found that higher amounts of glutamine in the media delayed the time until aspartate depletion, presumably corresponding to the time at which glutamine is fully depleted and unable to support further aspartate synthesis.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.

claim: Adding 1 mM asparagine delayed the decrease in sensor signal during glutamine limitation.
source: Furthermore, we found that adding 1 mM asparagine delayed the decrease in sensor signal, suggesting that when asparagine can be salvaged from the media it diverts glutamine consumption that would otherwise be purposed for asparagine synthesis via aspartate consumption.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.

claim: When asparagine can be salvaged from the media it diverts glutamine consumption that would otherwise be purposed for asparagine synthesis via aspartate consumption.
source: Furthermore, we found that adding 1 mM asparagine delayed the decrease in sensor signal, suggesting that when asparagine can be salvaged from the media it diverts glutamine consumption that would otherwise be purposed for asparagine synthesis via aspartate consumption.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of experimental data.

claim: For all three cell lines tested, there is a monotonically increasing relationship between sensor signal and intracellular aspartate concentration, covering around two orders of magnitude.
source: For all three cell lines, we observe a monotonically increasing relationship between sensor signal and intracellular aspartate concentration, covering around two orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation across multiple cell lines.

claim: There is no relationship between jAspSnFR3 sensor signal and intracellular glutamate levels.
source: We also observe no relationship between sensor signal and intracellular glutamate levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: The apparent cytosolic aspartate concentration is likely lower than the total aspartate concentration summed across all compartments.
source: We speculate that the apparent cytosolic aspartate concentration is likely lower than the total aspartate concentration summed across all compartments.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the observed discrepancy.

claim: The time to reach metabolic steady state after treatment can be much longer than 6-16 hr and depends on the treatment.
source: In most studies involving aspartate metabolism, metabolite extraction is performed 6–16 hr after treatment with the implicit assumption that this is enough time to reach metabolic steady state. Using our sensor, we have shown that the time to reach steady state can be much longer and depends on the treatment.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: A concurrently developed aspartate sensor based on SF-iGluSnFR was reported by another group.
source: Recently, a concurrently developed aspartate sensor based on SF-iGluSnFR was reported by another group (Hellweg et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to another study.

claim: The aspartate sensor by Hellweg et al. started with the S72A mutation and included six additional mutations identified by a combination of targeted screening and deep mutational scanning.
source: That aspartate sensor started with the S72A mutation, but then included six additional mutations identified by a combination of targeted screening and deep mutational scanning.
evidence: This is stated as a description of another group's work.

claim: jAspSnFR3 differs from the sensor by Hellweg et al. by 25 mutations.
source: Our design differs from the one by Hellweg et al., 2023 by 25 mutations (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between the two sensors.

claim: jAspSnFR3 achieved aspartate selectivity by generating only two mutations in the binding pocket of its precursor.
source: Notably, we achieved aspartate selectivity by generating only two mutations in the binding pocket of its precursor, and so the majority of these amino acid differences derive from us building off the next-generation precursor for iGluSnFR3, which has increased ΔF/F compared to iGluSnFR.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the engineering approach.

claim: jAspSnFR3 appears to have a larger signal change both in vitro and in live cells compared to the sensor by Hellweg et al.
source: Indeed, the sensor described here appears to have a larger signal change both in vitro and in live cells, although head-to-head comparisons have not been performed.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with a caveat about lack of direct comparison.

claim: jAspSnFR3 has a higher affinity for all three relevant ligands (aspartate, asparagine, and glutamate) compared to the sensor by Hellweg et al.
source: Another difference is that our jAspSnFR3 sensor has a higher affinity for all three relevant ligands (aspartate, asparagine, and glutamate); however, we found no discernible effect of treatment with 1 mM asparagine on sensor signal in cell culture experiments and found no correlation between intracellular glutamate concentration and sensor fluorescence across treatment conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with experimental validation.

claim: Treatment with 1 mM asparagine has no discernible effect on jAspSnFR3 sensor signal in cell culture experiments.
source: Another difference is that our jAspSnFR3 sensor has a higher affinity for all three relevant ligands (aspartate, asparagine, and glutamate); however, we found no discernible effect of treatment with 1 mM asparagine on sensor signal in cell culture experiments and found no correlation between intracellular glutamate concentration and sensor fluorescence across treatment conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is reported as an experimental observation.
